offerMemo.title: Offer memo
offerMemo.ownFundsNeededLine: Total own funds needed for this purchase price (indication): {value}.
offerMemo.offerLine: {amount} for the property at {address}, prepared on {date}.

tone.cautious: Cautious offer with both conditions in place; room to raise the bid if new information comes in.
tone.balanced: A realistic offer that matches what the public check shows.
tone.strong: Serious intent; a limited number of conditions, provided the documents support them.

conditions.financingWaived: No financing contingency; funding is (nearly) arranged. A bank guarantee or deposit is offered immediately.
conditions.inspectionRequired: Structural survey contingency (report follows within the agreed period).
conditions.inspectionWaived: No structural contingency; a recent survey report can be provided.

offerMemo.attentionFooter: These points come from public sources and are not a structural assessment; your own survey remains necessary.
offerMemo.nextStep1: If agreed, we would like to receive the draft purchase deed as soon as possible.
offerMemo.nextStep2: A bank guarantee or deposit will be arranged within 2 business days of verbal agreement.
offerMemo.nextStep3: A civil-law notary and appraiser have already been engaged for this property.
offerMemo.disclaimer: This memo was prepared by the buyer using WoonReality and is not advice, an appraisal, or a guarantee. Public data does not replace a survey, a civil-law notary, or mortgage advice.

reasons.noInspectionRisk: Without a survey contingency you carry the structural risk yourself.
reasons.noFinancingPenalty: Without a financing contingency you risk the 10% penalty if the bank does not go along.
reasons.aboveAskingPrice: Above the asking price: the bank lends based on the appraised value or the purchase price (whichever is lower). You must cover the difference from the appraised value out of your own pocket.

bidStrategy.cautiousReason1: Below the asking price because there is still uncertainty.
bidStrategy.cautiousReason2: Financing and survey contingencies stay in place.
bidStrategy.balancedAdjusted: Asking price corrected for attention points from the home check.
bidStrategy.balancedAtAskingPrice: Around the asking price, with both conditions precedent in place.
bidStrategy.balancedStarterSurvey: As a first-time buyer, a survey contingency is extra wise.
bidStrategy.balancedConditionsHold: Conditions keep the purchase reversible until the deadlines.
bidStrategy.strongCleanReason1: Only a small premium if the open data shows few red flags.
bidStrategy.strongCleanReason2: This is not a winning-chance prediction: bidding competition is unknown.
bidStrategy.strongIssuesReason: No markup above the asking price while attention points remain open.
bidStrategy.strongNoAnalysisReason1: Without a home analysis the offer stays at or below the asking price.
bidStrategy.strongNoAnalysisReason2: Financing and survey contingencies stay in place until the check is done.
bidStrategy.valuationNoteWithCosts: Not an appraisal. The asking price is what the seller asks, not what the home is worth. Indicative buyer's closing costs around {costs}.
bidStrategy.valuationNoteWithoutCosts: No appraisal and no Cadastre references. Enter the asking price; a market value only follows from official comparables or an appraiser.

riskSummary.one: {count} attention point from the open-data check{suffix}.
riskSummary.many: {count} attention points from the open-data check{suffix}.
riskSummary.none: No serious open-data attention points; the structural condition remains unknown without a survey.

negotiation.step1: React to one variable at a time: either the amount, or a condition (e.g. dropping a contingency). Never give away both in the same step.
negotiation.step2: Always ask what the reason behind the counteroffer is: another bid, an appraisal difference, or simply negotiating room. That determines your response.
negotiation.step3: Raise the bid in small, well-argued steps. Every increase without explanation suggests there is more room still.
negotiation.step4: Always put new agreements in writing (email), even if the seller's agent seems to agree verbally.
negotiation.escalationSummary: An escalation clause says: 'I bid X, but automatically go Y above the best competing bid, up to a maximum of Z.' This prevents you from having to blindly guess against unknown competition.
negotiation.escalationWhenToUse: Especially useful with demonstrable bidding competition (multiple viewers, short response window) and when you have a hard ceiling.
negotiation.escalationCaution: Agree beforehand with the selling agent that you receive the anonymised bid log afterwards, so you can verify the escalation was justified. Not every selling agent accepts this clause.
negotiation.walkAwayWithMax: Decide your maximum in advance (currently around {max}) and be prepared to walk away from the deal once it is exceeded. A house that costs you your financial margin is not a good buy.
negotiation.walkAwayWithoutMax: Decide your maximum in advance and be prepared to walk away from the deal once it is exceeded. A house that costs you your financial margin is not a good buy.

transferTax.label: Transfer tax
transferTax.noteInvestor: {rate}% for a property that is not a main residence ({year}). Not deductible.
transferTax.noteStarterExemption: First-time buyer exemption up to {threshold} ({year}; age, self-occupancy and prior use are verified by the civil-law notary). Not deductible.
transferTax.noteOwnerOccupier: {rate}% for a property as a main residence. Investment: {investorRate}%. The first-time buyer exemption depends on age and self-occupancy. Not deductible.
transferTax.noteNewBuild: New build (V.O.N.): VAT is included in the purchase price, no transfer tax.

notaryTransfer.label: Civil-law notary – deed of transfer (indication)
notaryTransfer.note: Deed transferring the property. Not deductible. Ask for a quote.

notaryMortgage.label: Civil-law notary – mortgage deed (indication)
notaryMortgage.note: Financing costs: deductible in box 1 in the year of payment.

kadasterTransfer.label: Cadastre – transfer registration
kadasterTransfer.note: Registration of the transfer ({year} KIK rate). Not deductible.

kadasterMortgage.label: Cadastre – mortgage registration
kadasterMortgage.note: Registration of the mortgage ({year} KIK rate). Deductible as financing costs.

appraisal.label: Appraisal (indication)
appraisal.note: Often required for the mortgage. Deductible if the appraisal is needed for the loan. Not a WoonReality valuation.

inspection.label: Structural survey (indication)
inspection.note: Optional but strongly recommended for older builds. Not deductible.

nhg.label: NHG guarantee fee
nhg.note: {rate}% of the mortgage amount ({year}; limit {limit}). Deductible. Often financed into the mortgage.

advice.label: Mortgage advice (indication)
advice.note: Advice and brokerage fees for the mortgage. Deductible in box 1. Ask for a quote.

bankGuarantee.label: Bank guarantee (indication)
bankGuarantee.note: Instead of paying a {percent}% deposit in cash. Not deductible.

moving.label: Moving costs (indication)
moving.note: No fixed fee; depends on distance and volume. Not deductible.

costs.disclaimer: This is a calculation sketch based on {year} parameters, not mortgage advice. Civil-law notary and adviser rates are indications; NHG, interest rates and bank conditions belong with a certified adviser.

gas.label: Gas
gas.note: ~{usage} m³/year × {price}/m³ + fixed costs. Includes heating, hot water and cooking.

water.label: Water
water.note: National average drinking water costs per household.

vve.label: VvE contribution
vve.note: Monthly contribution to the owners' association (from the listing).

municipalTaxes.label: Municipal taxes
municipalTaxes.note: Indication of property tax (OZB), sewerage charges and waste levies. Varies by municipality.

insurance.label: Buildings insurance
insurance.note: Indication based on {area} m² of living area.

runningCosts.disclaimer: This is an indication based on CBS averages and fixed estimates, not a personal quote. Actual costs depend on supplier, consumption, municipality and the property itself.

erfpacht.title: Leasehold: check the ground rent and term
erfpacht.summary: The listing mentions leasehold (erfpacht). That means a separate, often annual ground rent on top of your monthly payments, and it can affect mortgageability and value development.
erfpacht.action: Request the leasehold conditions: remaining term, ground rent, review date, and whether a buyout is possible or already done. Include this in your mortgage application.

vveReserveUnknown.title: VvE reserve fund not mentioned
vveReserveUnknown.summary: There is a VvE contribution, but no reserve fund is mentioned. Without a reserve you risk an unexpected special assessment.
vveReserveUnknown.action: Ask for the VvE documents (MJOP long-term maintenance plan, reserve fund, minutes) via the agent or civil-law notary.

vveSpecialLevy.title: Special levy or deferred maintenance mentioned
vveSpecialLevy.summary: The text mentions a special levy or deferred maintenance. This can be a significant extra cost on top of the purchase price.
vveSpecialLevy.action: Ask for the amount, the reason, and whether it has already been collected or is still to come.

ouderdomsclausule.title: Age clause mentioned
ouderdomsclausule.summary: An age clause limits what you can later recover from the seller for defects that fit the age of the property.
ouderdomsclausule.action: Have the civil-law notary review the exact clause wording before you sign.

asbest.title: Asbestos mentioned in the listing
asbest.summary: Asbestos is mentioned. Especially for builds before 1994 this matters for your structural survey.
asbest.action: Ask whether there is an asbestos inventory and consider discussing an asbestos clause with the civil-law notary.

vochtLekkage.title: Moisture, mould or leakage mentioned
vochtLekkage.summary: The listing text mentions moisture, mould or leakage. This is a concrete survey point.
vochtLekkage.action: Have the surveyor check this specifically and ask the seller for the repair history.

unreadable.title: Document barely readable
unreadable.summary: We could extract almost no text from this PDF. Scans without a text layer have to be handled manually.
unreadable.action: Upload a searchable PDF, or copy the key points into your notes yourself.

areaMismatch.title: Floor area differs from BAG
areaMismatch.summary: The document states about {advertised} m², BAG registers {registered} m². That is not a measurement error we may quietly ignore.
areaMismatch.action: Ask which measuring instruction the listing uses (NEN 2580) and whether storage/attic space was included.

priceMismatch.title: Purchase price differs from your offer
priceMismatch.summary: The deed states an amount around € {contract}; your offer draft is € {offer}.
priceMismatch.action: Put the deed next to your bid and ask the civil-law notary or agent about the difference.

mjopMissing.title: MJOP maintenance plan not clearly mentioned
mjopMissing.summary: No clear long-term maintenance plan was recognised in these VvE documents.
mjopMissing.action: Ask for the current MJOP and the latest general meeting minutes.

reserveFundUnclear.title: Reserve fund unclear
reserveFundUnclear.summary: The reserve fund was not recognised. That does not mean it is missing, but it does mean you need to verify it.
reserveFundUnclear.action: Ask for the reserve fund balance and whether a special assessment is coming.

questionnaireIncomplete.title: Questionnaire appears incomplete
questionnaireIncomplete.summary: Characteristic maintenance questions (roof, moisture, central heating, foundation) were not recognised.
questionnaireIncomplete.action: Review the questionnaire yourself and mark empty or evasive answers.

prewarFoundation.title: Foundation not explained for pre-war build
prewarFoundation.summary: BAG build year {year} and the documents do not mention the foundation. That is a gap, not a green flag.
prewarFoundation.action: Ask the seller for foundation research or known settlement.

moisture.title: Moisture or leakage mentioned
moisture.summary: The documents mention moisture, mould or leakage. That is a survey point, not a reason to ignore it.
moisture.action: Ask for photos and repair history, and have the surveyor look at it specifically.

foundation.title: Foundation risk in the text
foundation.summary: Foundation or subsidence is mentioned. Open data is not a foundation study.
foundation.action: Ask for a foundation report or a specialised inspection.

asbestos.title: Asbestos mentioned
asbestos.summary: Asbestos in the documents calls for a report or targeted survey, especially for builds before 1994.
asbestos.action: Ask whether there is an asbestos inventory and whether an asbestos clause is in the deed.

legalConflict.title: Legal conflict mentioned
legalConflict.summary: There appears to be a dispute, legal procedure or enforcement action in the documents.
legalConflict.action: Have the civil-law notary or a lawyer interpret the passage before you bid.

vveExtraCosts.title: Extra VvE costs or deferred maintenance
vveExtraCosts.summary: The text points to extra contributions or maintenance that has fallen behind.
vveExtraCosts.action: Ask for the MJOP maintenance plan, the reserve fund, and whether a special assessment has been decided.

ageClause.title: Age clause
ageClause.summary: An age clause limits the seller's liability for defects that fit the age of the property.
ageClause.action: Have the civil-law notary explain what you can and cannot recover.

leasehold.title: Leasehold or ground rent
leasehold.summary: Leasehold changes the monthly payments and saleability. BAG does not say whether the land is leasehold.
leasehold.action: Ask for the remaining term, the ground rent, and whether a buyout is possible.

mortgage.disclaimer: This is the statutory maximum under the 2026 lending norms, not mortgage advice and not a bank offer. Banks assess more strictly (documents, BKR registry, entrepreneurs often via IKV) and often land lower.

capacity.noIncome: Enter at least one income to calculate your borrowing capacity.

income.label: Test income
income.noteSingle: Gross test income according to the chosen income sources.

incomeLoan.label: Maximum mortgage from income
incomeLoan.note: Annuity over {years} years at the test rate.

singleExtra.label: Single-person supplement
singleExtra.note: Outside the financing burden up to {amount} (art. 3 paragraph 8).

energyPurchase.label: Energy label {label} extra
energyPurchase.noteTable: Extra borrowing room at purchase according to the 2026 table.

energyMeasures.label: Extra for sustainability measures
energyMeasures.note: Only usable for energy-saving measures; LTV up to 106%.

testRate.label: AFM test rate
testRate.note: Fixed-rate period under 10 years: tested against {rate}% ({basis}).

nhgCapped.label: NHG cap
nhgCapped.note: Income room of {room} capped at the {year} cost limit of {limit}{ebv}.

maxLoan.label: Maximum mortgage for purchase
maxLoan.notePlain: Sum of the income loan and purchase extras, after any NHG cap.

maxPrice.label: Maximum purchase price (before buyer's closing costs)
maxPrice.noteWithFunds: Mortgage for purchase {loan} + own funds {funds}. Transfer tax, civil-law notary and appraisal still need to come off this.
maxPrice.noteNoFunds: Without own funds this equals the maximum mortgage (LTV 100%) — buyer's closing costs cannot be paid out of it.

realBudget.label: What you can really spend
realBudget.note: The purchase price your own funds and mortgage room cover after transfer tax, civil-law notary, Cadastre, appraisal and survey. Use this amount to decide whether a house fits.

buyerCosts.label: Buyer's closing costs (indication)
buyerCosts.note: Transfer tax, civil-law notary, Cadastre, appraisal, survey and NHG fee where applicable. See the costs overview for deductibility.

ownFunds.label: Own funds
ownFunds.noteFallback: Contribution towards the purchase price and buyer's closing costs.

fundsGap.shortfallNote: Buyer's closing costs plus the part of the purchase price outside your maximum mortgage.
fundsGap.surplusNote: Your contribution covers the buyer's closing costs and any remainder of the purchase price (up to LTV 100%).

entrepreneur.label: Entrepreneur
entrepreneur.note: Test income = 3-year average, capped at the most recent year (NHG IKV). The bank usually requires an Entrepreneur's Income Statement.

scenarios.noLeaseNote: Currently {monthly} per month in the assessment.
scenarios.rateDownNote: Half a percent lower than your current test-rate input.
scenarios.rateUpNote: Half a percent higher than your current test-rate input.
scenarios.nhgWithoutNote: Cost limit {year} {limit}; income room may be higher.

lease.label: Private lease
lease.note: Actual monthly payment (NHG/BKR OA since April 2022, 100% of the contract).

student.label: Student loan
student.noteRemaining: {bracket} of the outstanding balance per month, because the DUO instalment is missing.
student.noteTerm: DUO instalment grossed up with factor {factor} (art. 3a).

revolving.label: Revolving credit / credit card
revolving.note: {percent}% of the limit per month (standard BKR RK assessment).

installment.label: Loans (car, personal)
installment.note: Actual monthly payment of repayment loans.

groundLease.label: Leasehold ground rent
groundLease.note: The annual ground rent counts as a financial obligation for this property.

alimony.label: Alimony
alimony.note: Partner and child alimony that you pay.

mortgage.taxDisclaimer: Mortgage interest deduction sketch {year}: maximum deduction rate {rate}%, including the imputed rental value (eigenwoningforfait). Net monthly payments are a year-1 indication. Not tax-filing advice.

affordability.emptyNoFinance: Fill in your mortgage calculator to see whether this house fits.
affordability.emptyNoPrice: Enter an asking price to see whether this house fits your budget.
affordability.noAskingPrice: After buyer's closing costs you can spend about {budget} on a house. Enter an asking price for a fit check.
affordability.fitsBase: This asking price fits, even after buyer's closing costs (budget {budget}).
affordability.renovationBuffer: About {value} in own funds left for renovation or buffer.
affordability.energyExtra: Plus {value} extra borrowing room solely for sustainability measures.
affordability.tight: Tight: after buyer's closing costs you are about {gap} short of your budget of {budget}. Extra own funds or a lower offer can close the gap.
affordability.over: Over your budget: this house costs {price}. After buyer's closing costs you can pay up to {budget} — {gap} short.
affordability.needOwnFunds: You need about {gap} in extra own funds for buyer's closing costs and your contribution.
affordability.fallback: What you can really spend according to your mortgage sketch: {budget}.
